items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When did you start playing some of those others, Jimmy Weston’s for example? I guess ’56, ’57.

ctx.x: Supper clubs are something that as a rule, don’t exist today like they did. Are there any other places that opened up as a result—are there any other sectors of the entertainment economy, or venues, that started booking the kinds of acts that the supper clubs used to?
The Copley Plaza, places like that. And the Village Vangate [Village Gate], the Village Vanguard. Some of the clubs on the West Side, Mikell’s Pub, Jimmy Weston’s.
When did you start playing some of those others, Jimmy Weston’s for example?
